edits.value_json: 你 means “you,” usually addressing one person. Its visible form combines 亻, the person-category element in one proposed analysis, and 尔, the simplified form of 爾, which was also used for “you/your.” The competing construction analyses remain unresolved; the proposed sound role of 尔 is not established by the modern readings alone.

你 means “you,” usually addressing one person. Its visible parts are 亻, treated as the person-category element in one proposed analysis, and 尔, the simplified form of 爾, also used for “you/your.” The formation remains disputed.
